question_text: Find dy and Δy for y = x² + x when x = 10 and Δx = 0.1.

mark_split.label: Find Δy from the exact change

recall_prompt: Say how you would do this one — say how you get dy, and say what makes Δy a different number.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Find dy from the derivative
steps.margin_note: First mark. Differentiate first, then multiply by Δx. Writing dy = (dy/dx)·Δx before any number goes in keeps this mark even if the arithmetic slips later.

recall.must_convey: That dy = (dy/dx)·Δx, with the derivative 2x + 1 found first and then multiplied by Δx.
accept: differentiate to get two x plus one and multiply by delta x
d y equals d y by d x times delta x
the derivative at ten is twenty one so d y is two point one
derivative teesi delta x tho multiply cheyyali
find d y by d x first then put x equals ten

steps.why: dy is not the change in y. It is the derivative multiplied by Δx — the straight-line estimate of that change — so the mark is for differentiating and then multiplying, in that order.
common_mistakes: Writing dy = 2x + 1 and leaving out the ·Δx.
Substituting Δx = 0.1 in place of x in the derivative.
steps.memory_tip: dy uses the derivative once. Δy uses the function twice. d for derivative, Δ for difference.

steps.label: Find Δy from the exact change
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Δy needs the function evaluated at both 10.1 and 10. Δx = 0.1 is large for this kind of question, so dy and Δy sit further apart here — 2.1 against 2.11.

lines.text: (Δy is the actual change in y)

recall.must_convey: That Δy = f(x + Δx) − f(x) = f(10.1) − f(10) = 2.11, the exact change.
accept: delta y is f of ten point one minus f of ten
the exact change is two point one one
rendu values lo substitute chesi subtract cheyyali
delta y is the real change and d y is only the estimate

steps.why: Δy is the real change in y, so the function has to be worked out at both points. The gap between dy and Δy is 0.01 here, and it grows as Δx grows — which is why the approximation is only used for small Δx.
common_mistakes: Stopping at dy when the question asks for both numbers.
steps.memory_tip: Δy is the after value minus the before value, in that order — a negative Δy is allowed and simply means y went down.

insider_note: Δx = 0.1 is comparatively large here, so dy and Δy differ visibly — 2.1 against 2.11. That visible gap is the point of the question.
